chapterTitle: English Unit 2: Phrases & Clauses (Noun, Adjective, Adverbial, Appositive & Prepositional)
subject: english

questions.question: She hopes that she will travel around the world someday.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Noun clause. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: We stayed in a house near to the canal.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Adverb phrase. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Laws were quickly passed so that the child abuse could be checked.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Adverbial clause. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: A repetition of the same word or phrase at the beginning of a line throughout the work is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (D) Anaphora. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Marty, the class clown, made everyone laugh with his funny gestures.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Appositive phrase. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Identify the phrase exemplifying the most appropriate order of adjectives.
questions.explanation: According to the Royal Order of Adjectives (OSASCOMP), Opinion ('expensive') precedes Age ('new'), which precedes Origin ('imported'): 'An expensive, new, imported car.'

questions.question: In the sentence "They elected her captain of the debate team," what is the function of the phrase "captain of the debate team"?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Object complement. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: "What a brilliant idea you had last night." This sentence is technically:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Exclamatory but declarative in form. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: What is "anaphora"?

options.A: The repetition of the same consonant sounds at the beginning of words.
options.B: The repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses.
options.C: A reference to another work or event.
options.D: A type of irony in which the outcome is opposite of what is expected.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) The repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: What is the term for the repetition of a consonant sound at the beginning of words in a line or phrase?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Alliteration. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the phrase "the United Nations"?

options.A: The United Nations is a global organization.
options.B: The United Nations are a global organization.
options.C: The United Nations have a global organization.
options.D: The United Nations is global organization.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) The United Nations is a global organization.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the comma to separate a non-restrictive clause correctly?

options.A: My brother, who lives in Paris, is visiting next week.
options.B: My brother who lives in Paris, is visiting next week.
options.C: My brother who lives in Paris is visiting next week.
options.D: My brother, who lives in Paris is visiting next week.

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) My brother, who lives in Paris, is visiting next week.. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence, "John, who had never been to Paris before, went to see it," the phrase 'who had never been to Paris before' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Cataphora. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: The phrase "although it was raining" in the sentence "Although it was raining, she went for a walk" is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Adverbial adjunct. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence, "The man sitting in the chair is my uncle," the phrase 'sitting in the chair' is a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Adverbial adjunct. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: The cataphora in the sentence "Before he left, John packed his bag" refers to:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) The subject of the sentence. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence, "The book on the table is mine," the noun phrase "the book on the table" serves as a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Subject. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: The phrase "in the garden" in the sentence "The children are playing in the garden" is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Adjunct. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: The phrase "I wish he were here" is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Subjunctive mood. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence "Although it was late, he continued to work," the word "although" introduces a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Subordinate clause. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: The phrase "the food on the table" in the sentence "The food on the table is delicious" is a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Noun phrase. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: The word "even though" in the sentence "Even though it was late, she finished the project" introduces a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Subordinate clause. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence, "If he had studied, he would have passed the test," the subordinate clause is:

options.A: He would have passed the test

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) If he had studied. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence "The man, who was sitting quietly, spoke to me," the clause 'who was sitting quietly' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) A relative clause. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence "The man who wore the red shirt won the race," the phrase "who wore the red shirt" is an example of:

options.A: A restrictive clause modifying the noun man
options.C: A non-restrictive clause modifying the noun man
options.D: A gerund phrase modifying the noun man

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) A restrictive clause modifying the noun man. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence "The book, which was on the table, is mine," the clause "which was on the table" is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) A non-restrictive clause. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Identify the noun phrase in the sentence: "The book on the shelf is mine."
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) The book on the shelf. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence "The man reading the newspaper in the park is my uncle," the phrase "reading the newspaper in the park" is a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Participle phrase. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains a restrictive clause?

options.A: "My friend, who lives in New York, is coming tomorrow."
options.B: "The woman who called earlier is my sister."
options.C: "The car, which was parked outside, is mine."
options.D: "The cat, which you adore, is outside."

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) "The woman who called earlier is my sister.". This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.

questions.question: In the sentence "I have a project to complete," the phrase "to complete" is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) An infinitive phrase. This conforms to official FBISE English HSSC-I standards for Phrases and Clauses Analysis.
